title: Corpus Portability & Artifact Sensitivity
flagsIntroducedNote: EMPTY by design, not by omission. outstandingFindings.summary: No feature flag is declared. G111 requires an introduced flag to be default-OFF in every non-owning train's bundle, which requires editing config/feature-flags.mvp.yaml — owned by bubbles.train and outside this run's permitted surface. flagsIntroduced is deliberately empty rather than falsely populated.

The manifest's initial record-class list is not fixed by spec.md. It must be derived from the store rather than hand-listed, or it will be incomplete on the day it is written — which is the original defect reproduced in a new location.

Spec 110 introduces passages, a second copy of user content, and routes their portability here via F-110-EGRESS-01. If 110 lands first, the manifest must include passages from its first version. The ordering between the two specs is a real dependency.

The egress decision consumes grants that spec 108 defines and enforces. Spec 108 targets the same 'next' train and is specs_hardened, not delivered. SCOPE-08 cannot execute before 108's grant model exists.

Persisting sensitivity leaves every existing artifact unset, and R-111-25 makes unset a refusal. Enabling the fail-closed gate without a backfill or a declared migration posture would refuse legitimate existing traffic. The migration posture must be an explicit decision.

The authoring brief required conformance to .specify/templates/spec-template.md; that file does not exist in this repository (.specify/templates/ is absent; the template exists only in sibling workspace repositories). spec.md follows the adjacent spec's structure and the Bubbles BDD scenario contract instead. Either the template should be installed or the instruction corrected.

Deletion interacts with records derived from artifacts (relationships, summaries, collections). Whether deleting an artifact deletes, orphans, or rewrites its derivatives is undecided and affects both delete correctness and round-trip parity.

Canonical content hash per record class requires a defined serialisation order and field set per class. Undefined, parity comparison is not reproducible across instances, so SCOPE-05 cannot be specified.

executionHistory.releaseTrainRationale: Chose 'next' (target_slot staging) over 'mvp' (target_slot prod) on four grounds. (1) This introduces a fail-closed enforcement point — the same change class spec 108 explicitly declared 'next' for in its own words: 'security-posture change; MUST NOT ship on mvp'. (2) The egress decision consumes spec 108's grants, which are themselves on 'next'; shipping the gate on 'mvp' would split one security posture across two trains and have the gate validate a grant vocabulary the mvp train does not enforce. (3) Whole-corpus deletion is irreversible, and proving export-import-delete parity on staging before exposing corpus erasure on the live self-hosted host is the correct order for a capability whose failure mode is permanent data loss. (4) Persisting sensitivity leaves every existing artifact unset, and unset is a refusal, so enabling this against a live corpus before the F-111-BACKFILL-01 migration posture is decided would refuse legitimate traffic. The honest cost of this choice — that the mvp train remains non-conformant with Principle 11's unconditional-exit guarantee until promotion — is stated explicitly in spec.md rather than obscured by the train choice.

executionHistory.g094ShapeRationale: Chose the PROPORTIONATE shape (Single-Capability Justification + Single-Implementation Justification) over the heavy Capability Foundation / Concrete Implementations / Variation Axes split, on four grounds. (1) The gate applied on a single trigger hit: the word 'provider' occurs once in spec.md section 4, inside a sentence arguing that provider-first modelling would recreate the divergence this feature exists to remove. That is an argument against a provider abstraction, not evidence of one. (2) The guard measured concreteImplementationEntries=0; there is no set of two or more interchangeable implementations of one contract. Export, import and delete are three operations resolving scope from ONE manifest (P1), not three providers of one interface. (3) spec.md forecloses the two places a provider layer could appear: Non-Goal 1 forbids a second export path, and R-111-27 requires a single egress chokepoint. (4) Declaring a foundation split would have been fabrication: design.md records eight open decisions (D1-D8), three behind BLOCKING findings, so any foundation, implementation set, or variation axis written today would be invention presented as a chosen architecture. The design.md justification states explicitly what would reopen the question — if D7 or D1 resolve into two or more interchangeable implementations, the split becomes required and belongs to bubbles.design.
executionHistory.checkEightBIncident: The first Test Plan draft labelled the regression rows 'Regression E2E (e2e-api)'. On SCOPE-06's row the token 'api' landed within the 160-character window of the word 'removes', which matched Check 8B's rename/removal trigger and raised three consumer-trace findings on a spec that renames and removes nothing. Spec 111 ADDS delete surfaces (E6 records that no corpus delete surface exists today) and corrects the existing export in place; no route, path, endpoint or contract identity changes. Writing a Consumer Impact Sweep would therefore have documented a change that is not happening in order to satisfy a gate. The incidental word collision was removed instead ('removes only its scope' -> 'erases only its own scope') and the check correctly returned to not-applicable.
